thisSessionNoteAccount.point: 2 - absence disclosure versus the syntax guard precedence
thisSessionNoteAccount.how: UNAVAILABLE_RELEASE_DISCLOSURE is replaced by UNDECLARED_CAPABILITY_ACCOUNT, which is deliberately NOT Coverage-shaped: it carries declared/candidateDeficiency/candidateNativeCause/subjectToPrecedence, never coverage/deficiency/nativeCause. Controls: the-absence-account-is-not-shaped-like-a-coverage-result, language-tier-unsupported-outranks-provider-unavailable-in-the-published-precedence, the-absence-account-marks-its-deficiency-as-subject-to-precedence-not-as-the-outcome, an-undeclared-and-unservable-capability-keeps-the-more-specific-derived-pair, the-owning-syntax-derivation-still-refuses-a-substituted-release-pair. The existing guard is not weakened.

Each absence row now carries an explicit `projection`: `coverage-entry` with the exact relation@rung coordinates for fact-producing capabilities, and `selection-account-only` with empty relations for clones-near and clones-cross-tsjs, which are candidate-only by section 6.1 authority and mint no fact, no relation@rung and therefore no CoverageResultV3. The law says an availability account may be shared but is automatically a Coverage result for none of them. Controls: candidate-only-capabilities-have-no-relation-and-project-to-no-coverage, a-candidate-only-absence-is-a-selection-account-not-a-coverage-entry, a-fact-producing-absence-names-the-exact-relation-at-rung-it-projects-onto.
